messages:
jordan: pasted an nsys run from last night's perf job — spikes on kernel 0x7f (fused_attn_forward) and a correlated burst of KV-store write activity, here's the TL;DR: 30ms tail on batch=8 seq=2048, avg token latency 12ms -> 45ms tail.
jordan: attaching the trace snippet I looked at: `nsys profile --output=tmp/kv-throttle-305 --trace=cuda,cublas,cudnn ./run_infer`. Perf map shows repeated kernel requeueing.
maria: can you paste the perfetto timeline or a screenshot? quick eyes might spot concurrent memcpy or stream syncs. :eyes:
jordan: perfetto snippet pasted inline below (cropped):
```
GPU timeline:
- 00:00:00.000 fused_attn_fwd kernel (SMs 90% occupancy)
- 00:00:00.022 kv_write_async (copy to device)
- 00:00:00.024 fused_attn_fwd (relaunch, shorter)
- 00:00:00.048 fused_attn_fwd (long tail)
- 00:00:00.050 kv_write_sync (stall)
```
cheng: looks like write-after-read churn in our kvcache path; writes are happening during inference windows. Might be our async write path hitting backpressure when batch inter-arrival bursts are uneven.
eli: did we see L2 or DRAM counter blips? also are these fused kernels using sharedmem heavily?
jordan: nsys counters: L2 util spikes, DRAM bw high during the write bursts, shared mem bw steady. SM warp efficiency drops just before the long tail.
maria: could be coalesced writes turning into many small transactions — check our kvcache flush granularity + allocator churn. Also our kernel selector currently prefers fused_attn when seq_len >= 1024 unless heuristics suggest tiled_attn; maybe fused_attn reopened more frequently because of kv write interrupts.
perf-bot: automated summary: "nsys: repeated kernel preemption/queueing observed. Top kernels: fused_attn_fwd (46%), kvcache_write_async (18%), memcpy_htod_async (12%). Suggest instrumenting stream assignment and backpressure on kvcache writer."
jordan: experiment idea: route kvcache writes to a dedicated low-priority stream and add a small coalesce window (2-4ms) to reduce write bursts. Also try forcing fused_attn -> tiled_attn for batch<=8, seq>=1536 to see if behavior changes.
cheng: quick A/B plan:
- A: baseline (current selector)
- B: funnel writes to stream 3 (low-prio), coalesce window 3ms
- C: selector override -> tiled_attn for edge case, same write funneling
We can run each for 2k requests and compare p50/p95/p99.
maria: add nvprof counters for atomic/serialize stalls and issue_replay to validate whether writes are causing pipeline bubbles. Use `nvprof --metrics inst_executed,stall_reason,issue_replay` snippet.
jordan: I ran a quick micro: forcing tiled_attn dropped p99 from 45ms->28ms for the same workload, but p50 stayed similar. So fused_attn seems sensitive to KV write interruption patterns.
eli: interesting — maybe fused_attn's kernel launches are longer and more preemptible; tiled attn breaks the work into smaller kernels so interference is less costly. We should update kernel selector heuristic: prefer shorter-kernel variants when concurrent device-side IO > X%.
cheng: implementation notes: add a metric in the runtime for "device-write-burst-rate" sampled over 100ms windows. If > threshold, prefer partitioned kernels or limit concurrent fused launches.
jordan: logging plan: emit per-request tag: selector_decision, device_write_burst_rate, kvcache_write_coalesced (bool). Keep as trace fields in console so workbooks can correlate.
maria: potential regression risk: tiled_attn increases CPU-side scheduling and may bump cost. We'll add cost-sensitivity flag so enterprise tiers can pin behavior.
perf-bot: request: schedule perfetto+nsys combo for the A/B run. Endpoint: /perf/run/kv-throttle-305 with tags ["kvcache-funnel", "selector-overrides"].
eli: one more check: are HBM pressure metrics on the host visible? on some cards HBM eviction can spike latencies even w/o obvious DRAM bw. If available, capture `nvidia-smi dmon` during runs.
jordan: summary action items:
- Cheng: implement write-funnel + coalesce window (stream 3) experiment (ETA: today)
- Maria: add nvprof metrics and perfetto template for A/B (ETA: EOD)
- Eli: add device-write-burst-rate metric and runtime flag (ETA: tomorrow)
- Jordan: run A/B and upload traces to perf bucket, annotate p50/p95/p99 (ETA: tomorrow noon)
Everyone: react to this thread with :thumbsup: if you agree or DM if you want to be on the run.
